title: Reject shell metacharacters in test code_spec
problem: runner/executor.py runs test-action code_spec via subprocess.run(shell=True). validate_plan's existing _check_test_code_spec_format only rejects prose starters, so a code_spec like 'python -m unittest foo; rm -rf /' passes validation (first word is 'python') and then executes literally. Shell injection from a buggy or compromised planner is fully unblocked.
description:
Add a new check in runner/validate_plan.py — either a new helper _check_test_shell_metacharacters or extend _check_test_code_spec_format — that rejects any test-action step whose code_spec contains shell metacharacters that enable command chaining, redirection, or substitution.

Reject if the code_spec contains any of:
  ;  &  |  >  <  `  $(  ${

Allow normal command syntax: alphanumerics, spaces, dashes, underscores, dots, slashes, equals, single and double quotes, brackets [ ], parentheses (only when not part of $()), and the dot-stem characters needed for module paths.

Implementation note: a denylist of dangerous metachars is simpler and safer than an allowlist of safe chars; the latter would reject legitimate things like '--flag=value with space'.

Wire the new check into validate() alongside the existing test code_spec checks.

Add tests covering: clean command (python -m unittest x.y) passes; semicolon (python -m unittest x; rm -rf /) rejected; backtick substitution (python -c `whoami`) rejected; pipe (python -m unittest | tee log) rejected; redirect (python -m unittest > /dev/null) rejected; ampersand background (python -m unittest &) rejected; $() substitution rejected; double-quoted argument with space (python -c "import x") still passes.
context: Filed as scribe TODO #238. Security hardening — protects against a buggy or compromised planner emitting destructive shell commands as test steps. Self-contained validate_plan addition; no executor changes.
